attributes.residual: 26 lines, two clusters, and this pass changed the CLASSIFICATION of both. CLUSTER A (20 lines, the 80-row loop): now provably a SINGLE consistent 4-cycle renaming sigma = (r20 r22 r21 r23). Before this pass only 5 of its 9 words fitted sigma; the four reload-block words broke the bijection because ours coalesced the v36 reload in place into q36's dying register (lwz r21,0(r21)) where the target keeps v36 in its own register (lwz r20,0(r22)). Splitting the reload into its own local makes all NINE words fit sigma exactly - verified word by word. This CORRECTS attempt.webfrank-closure2.initeffects, which flagged cluster A as a clean recolor candidate: it was NOT one at the time, and it only becomes one under the w36 source form. CLUSTER B (6 lines): the three stores at +0x5d4/+0x63c/+0x69c where retail folds stw r0,1068(r31)/1140/1152 and we emit stw r0,0(r23)/0(r20)/0(r19). SOURCE-DEAD with a named mechanism (use-count-driven allocator priority re-ranking, above), and NOT postprocessor-eligible because the difference is an instruction immediate. ALSO FALSIFIED HERE: that record's proposed next action, 'drop the three single-use base locals so the displacement folds', is wrong - the locals are NOT single-use and NOT absent from the target. fnasm shows all twelve pointer materializations at 0x1fc-0x228 byte-identical INCLUDING addi r23,r31,1068, and the else-arm store stw r3,0(r23) and test lwz r0,0(r23) both match. Deleting those locals would break the else arms. NET VERDICT on the lane's WEBFRANK-READY question: NO. Cluster B's immediates keep the function ineligible whatever cluster A does, so the w36 form buys no score today and was NOT retained (see scope).
